materials.note: Locomotive cinders as track ballast, filled up round the ties: coarse clinker in a fine black-grey ash, a few rust-brown and glassy lumps and pale ash where the sun has dried it. The darkness and fineness are what both Glessner photographs at 18th Street show; grain and colour are reconstructed (L-ic-tracks-2478).

materials.note: The top of an untreated hewn-oak crosstie a few seasons in the track, weathered silver-brown: grain along its length, end and season checks, cinder dust packed into the grain and a darker band where each rail sits. Untreated because creosoting was still unusual on Midwestern lines before about 1910; that, the wood and its colour are reconstructed (L-ic-tracks-2478).
